Chapter 7: The Wisdom of Groundlessness
You know, there’s a certain comfort in thinking we can control life.
Maybe you’ve felt it—that belief that, if you just work hard enough, everything will fall into place. But sooner or later, we all face moments when the ground just... disappears.
Plans unravel, relationships shift, health takes unexpected turns.
And in those moments? Your mind scrambles, desperate to grab onto something solid. But nothing feels certain.
Let me share a story.
There was a young professional who’d spent years carefully planning her career. She was so sure about that big promotion—she could almost see it. But then, just like that, it slipped away. The disappointment hit hard, but underneath it was a deeper fear: not knowing what comes next.
For days, she tried to get back on track, searching for answers, looking for guarantees. But the more she grasped, the more slippery stability became.
Then, one day, she stopped. She noticed the tension in her body, her racing thoughts. And she realized something: the discomfort wasn’t just about the lost opportunity—it was about losing that sense of certainty.
So, she let herself feel that groundlessness.
She stopped looking for immediate answers. It was unsettling, sure... but also, strangely freeing.
Most of us spend our lives trying to avoid groundlessness. We tell ourselves that happiness depends on knowing and controlling what’s coming. But here’s something to pay attention to: life is always changing, always uncertain.
The tighter we hold on, the more anxious and rigid we get. But when you learn to relax into groundlessness, when you stop needing control all the time, something new opens up—a different kind of freedom.
Think about a retiree, facing all the unknowns of aging. Instead of fighting the uncertainty, she finds comfort in simply noticing each moment as it arrives—not trying to predict or control the future.
The uncertainty is still there, but it’s less scary. There’s more space, more willingness to meet life just as it is.
The wisdom of groundlessness isn’t about giving up or becoming passive.
It’s seeing that real security doesn’t come from outside circumstances. It comes from your ability to stay present and open—even when nothing feels certain.
That’s the heart of resilience—the courage and curiosity to meet whatever life brings, one moment at a time.
